idiom_name: serialisable command object + transport frame + invoker that deserialises and calls execute()
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define a narrow command contract (a stable type tag plus an execution entry point) and concrete commands that carry their parameters as data; serialise the command into the transport's frame with the tag included, and let a receiver-side invoker reconstruct the concrete command and invoke its entry point. Keep the tag-to-implementation mapping in an explicit allow-list registry so the invoker never instantiates a type named by the payload, and keep commands data-only: references to receivers, handles or live connections cannot cross the boundary, so the far side resolves them from the payload. Design the wire contract first (tag names, field evolution, unknown-field tolerance) and deploy both sides from it.
code_sketch:
# client
payload = codec.encode(cmd)                 # {tag: "render", fields...}
transport.send(payload)

# invoker (far side)
while frame := transport.receive():
    tag, fields = codec.decode(frame)       # the tag is data, never trusted
    handler = registry.lookup(tag)
    if handler is None:
        dead_letter(frame)
        continue
    handler(fields).execute()
pitfalls: Deserialising a command is executing data: without an allow-list of tags and a safe codec, an unauthorised producer on the queue can run arbitrary code.
Data-only rule: a command that serialises a receiver reference or an open resource drags the object graph across the boundary and fails on the far side.
No at-least-once plan: duplicate execution, poison messages and a missing dead-letter path are the normal failure modes, not edge cases.

Wrong move: resolving the command tag through reflection or dynamic loading over the payload's class name -> adding a jar or assembly, or any unauthorised producer on the queue, silently becomes a remote-code-execution surface -> instead map tags to handlers in an explicit allow-list and dead-letter every unknown tag.

Wrong move: putting rich domain objects or ORM entities into the command payload -> serialisation drags the whole object graph across, or the worker acts on state that changed while the command queued -> instead pass ids and primitive data and re-fetch on the far side, the rule Sidekiq's docs enforce for perform arguments.

Wrong move: leaning on transport retries with non-idempotent handlers -> at-least-once delivery duplicates every side effect (double charge, double email) on each replay -> instead key idempotency to a business identifier and de-duplicate at the receiver before executing.
